candidates.title: Semantic receipts and evidence order in belief updating
candidates.mechanism: A semantic provenance receipt may change how an agent weights the first of two otherwise matched signals, producing an order interaction rather than a generic source-label effect.

theory.game: A controlled sequential belief-reporting game with two matched signals and randomized receipt and order assignments.
theory.players: One reporting agent and a scripted information source.
theory.actions: Report a posterior probability after each signal and a final posterior.
theory.information_structure: Signal content is fixed across arms; only semantic receipt and presentation order are randomized.
theory.solution_concept: Bayesian updating under a fixed likelihood model is the scripted benchmark.
theory.benchmark: The receipt-minus-placebo difference in first-signal carryover is zero.
theory.prediction: The candidate mechanism predicts a nonzero receipt by first-signal-order interaction.
theory.falsifier: The preregistered interaction interval stays inside the declared negligible-effect band.
theory.predeclared_decision_rule: Advance only if the interaction clears the frozen effect and robustness thresholds; otherwise stop this mechanism.

experiment.benchmark: Scripted Bayesian posterior updates under the same two signals.

arms.treatment: Semantic receipt with signal A presented first.
Semantic receipt with signal B presented first.
Matched placebo receipt with signal A presented first.
Matched placebo receipt with signal B presented first.

sample_plan.unit: One independently reset scripted game transcript.
sample_plan.missingness: Count every attempted transcript; invalid or missing reports remain in the denominator.

experiment.outcome: Final posterior carryover interaction, with intermediate posteriors retained as diagnostics.
experiment.falsifier: No interaction outside the frozen negligible-effect band under both order codings.

applied.data: Scripted signals, receipts, order assignments, and posterior reports.
applied.as_of: Raw candidate design as of 2026-09-25; no study data have been collected.
applied.measurement: Receipt by order interaction on posterior carryover.
applied.limitation: C1 remains stopped at insufficient_full_text_binding; this card does not clear that source gate.

prior_work.summary: Source identity is pinned, but scientific merit is not established. The C1 disposition retains four negative neighbors, two abstract-only unknowns, and the stop code insufficient_full_text_binding.

sources.claim: The owner brief defines the required candidate-card fields and separates candidate generation from later selection.

sources.locator: ## What I decided, and what I deliberately did not
sources.claim: The disposition records retained evidence and the unresolved C1 stop condition without making a gate or novelty decision.
The exact-claim matrix distinguishes adjacent mechanisms from the receipt by order estimand and leaves decisive full-text cells unknown.

anomaly_branches.outcome: A source-label main effect appears without the order interaction.
anomaly_branches.next_hypothesis: Receipt semantics alter baseline trust but not sequential weighting.

anomaly_branches.outcome: The interaction reverses between signal-content pairs.
anomaly_branches.next_hypothesis: Semantic content or difficulty, rather than provenance, moderates the apparent order effect.

reasons.p_pass_t: The factorial contrast is crisp, but the decisive prior-art binding is incomplete.
reasons.p_pass_s: A clean interaction would still require independent source and novelty review.
reasons.p_pass_a: The current card names no validated applied deployment path.
reasons.p_dead_end: The retained negative neighbors and inaccessible decisive texts create a material stop risk.
reasons.interest_0_10: The mechanism directly studies how information provenance and order shape beliefs.

candidates.title: Information-constrained adapters in repeated belief games
candidates.mechanism: An adapter with explicitly limited observations may trade off own-state fidelity against partner-state prediction under one normalized payoff, creating a testable gap between general and partner-specific policies.

theory.game: A finite repeated binary-action game with fully specified transition, observation, and payoff equations.
theory.players: One focal adapter and one scripted partner drawn from a frozen type set.
theory.actions: Choose one binary action per round from the information exposed by the declared adapter.
theory.information_structure: The focal policy sees only the declared current state and lagged partner observation; hidden state remains unavailable.
theory.solution_concept: Exact enumeration over one common policy class and every optimizer tie.
theory.benchmark: The identity policy and per-partner policies evaluated in the same normalized units.
theory.prediction: A genuinely new equation-complete information constraint may produce a positive lower tie-envelope gap.
theory.falsifier: Any declared parameter value has a lower tie-envelope gap below the frozen threshold.
theory.predeclared_decision_rule: Enumerate only after every equation and policy domain is frozen; stop if any required parameter misses the threshold.

experiment.benchmark: Exact identity-policy payoff under the same dynamics and normalization.

arms.treatment: One general policy is selected across every partner type.
One policy is selected separately for each partner type under the same score.
The frozen identity mapping is evaluated as a control.

sample_plan.unit: One exact state-history and partner-type cell.
sample_plan.missingness: Enumeration must cover every declared cell and optimizer tie; any omitted cell invalidates the result.

experiment.outcome: Lower optimizer-tie envelope of the normalized general-versus-typed policy gap.
experiment.falsifier: The envelope is nonpositive or below threshold at any predeclared parameter.

applied.venue: Offline exact enumerator for a synthetic repeated game.
applied.data: Declared state histories, partner types, equations, policies, and payoff table.
applied.as_of: Raw replacement candidate as of 2026-09-25; no preregistration exists.
applied.measurement: Exact normalized payoff gap over all optimizer ties.
applied.limitation: The accepted C3 screen stops the older instrument; this separate raw card still needs an equation-complete review.

prior_work.summary: Source identity is pinned, but scientific merit is not established. The later C3 screen's stop and no-preregistration disposition supersedes the older choice; this card cannot inherit the older instrument's status.

sources.claim: The older choice records the frozen-solo adapter proposal and its intended predicate; it is historical input, not current clearance.
The prior-art matrix records an algebraic collision and limits what can be inferred about narrower alternatives.
The later screen records stop and no preregistration for the current C3 instrument and requires any continuation to be genuinely new and equation-complete.

anomaly_branches.outcome: The identity policy is optimal for every partner under the new equations.
anomaly_branches.next_hypothesis: The information restriction is behaviorally inert in the declared game.

anomaly_branches.outcome: A positive gap depends on selecting one favorable optimizer tie.
anomaly_branches.next_hypothesis: The apparent effect is tie-selection instability rather than a robust mechanism.

reasons.p_pass_t: An equation-complete replacement is testable, but the nearby identity-policy no-go is strong.
reasons.p_pass_s: Even a positive exact gap would need a separate collision and interpretation review.
reasons.p_pass_a: The synthetic game has no demonstrated application mapping.
reasons.p_dead_end: Common-class algebra and optimizer-tie requirements may eliminate the proposed gap.
reasons.interest_0_10: The card connects information constraints to strategic adaptation without treating the stopped C3 design as valid.

candidates.title: Prospective information cutoffs and market-belief calibration
candidates.mechanism: Freezing an information cutoff, contemporaneous quote, and abstention rule before resolution may separate genuine belief calibration from hindsight and near-resolution price leakage.

theory.game: A sequential forecasting game against a contemporaneous market-implied probability.
theory.players: One paper forecaster and a market baseline; no capital-executing player is included.
theory.actions: Issue a timestamped probability forecast or a recorded abstention before a frozen cutoff.
theory.information_structure: Only information receipted before the cutoff and the contemporaneous quote snapshot are visible.
theory.solution_concept: Proper-score minimization with abstentions retained in coverage.
theory.benchmark: The contemporaneous market-implied probability under the same event and timestamp.
theory.prediction: A source-bound prospective protocol may improve calibrated probability error without relying on resolved-market leakage.
theory.falsifier: Out-of-sample score does not improve over the frozen market baseline or the effect disappears under timing placebo.
theory.predeclared_decision_rule: Report negative or unknown unless source, timing, coverage, and cost gates all pass on the sealed window.

experiment.benchmark: Contemporaneous market-implied forecast captured at the same cutoff.

arms.treatment: Forecast uses only receipted pre-cutoff information.
Apply the frozen method to a shifted cutoff that should not improve information.

sample_plan.unit: One independently resolved event with a valid pre-cutoff snapshot.
sample_plan.missingness: Retain abstentions, unresolved events, quote failures, and source outages with explicit denominators.

experiment.outcome: Brier-score difference and coverage, with paper-value diagnostics reported separately.
experiment.falsifier: No score improvement on the sealed events, or improvement fails timing and source-placebo checks.

applied.data: Pre-cutoff source receipts, event rules, quote snapshots, forecasts, abstentions, and later outcomes.
applied.as_of: Proposed protocol only as of 2026-09-25; the cited exp007 result is retrospective and mock.
applied.measurement: Out-of-sample calibration against the contemporaneous market baseline with full coverage accounting.
applied.limitation: The applied documents are proposals, and exp007 provides no prospective edge or live-trading evidence.

prior_work.summary: Source identity is pinned, but scientific merit is not established. The applied audit and plan are proposed designs; exp007 is a deterministic mock and retrodictive paper exercise.

sources.claim: The audit proposes prospective capture and a sidecar evidence path while explicitly withholding claims that the strategy works.
The plan proposes a chronological sealed design with full attempt denominators and separate empirical gates.
The experiment note identifies the checked-in run as an offline deterministic mock rather than prospective evidence.

anomaly_branches.outcome: Calibration improves but paper-value diagnostics do not.
anomaly_branches.next_hypothesis: Probability accuracy is real but insufficient to overcome venue prices, fees, or timing.

anomaly_branches.outcome: The apparent gain disappears when unresolved and abstained events remain in the denominator.
anomaly_branches.next_hypothesis: Selective coverage, rather than information quality, generated the apparent improvement.

reasons.p_pass_t: The prospective cutoff and scoring contract are directly falsifiable.
reasons.p_pass_s: Known forecasting methods reduce theory novelty, while the source-bound application question remains open.
reasons.p_pass_a: A read-only paper protocol could yield evidence, but no prospective result exists.
reasons.p_dead_end: Coverage, resolution lag, and a strong market baseline may leave the result negative or unknown.
reasons.interest_0_10: The design connects information discipline, belief calibration, and an applied strategic baseline.
